title: Feasibility, acceptability, and effectiveness of online MST for psychosis and online D-MST for depression: a pilot study.
summary:
The study to be registered aims to test the feasibility and effectiveness of psychotherapeutic group interventions in the form of online metacognitive training for psychosis (MCT), as well as for depression (D-MCT) in the outpatient setting. This therapeutic offer can be a valuable addition to the existing psychiatric care landscape, especially since severely mentally ill patients sometimes only receive adequate support after a longer course of illness. The reasons for this are manifold, whereby on the one hand negative expectations or inhibitions on the part of those affected can play a role.
Furthermore, socioeconomic and structural circumstances can also make access to therapeutic help more difficult. In an effort to overcome said barriers, MCT and D-MCT are offered online. Easier access and the possibility of anonymity can also make it easier to persuade people who are worried about stigmatization to participate. Furthermore, thanks to the group setting and the manageable time frame, interested individuals can be treated promptly. In this way, significant progress can be made in treatment and, if necessary, waiting times for conventional inpatient or outpatient therapy places can be bridged. The playful format is also intended to reduce prejudices against psychotherapy among therapy-critical participants and to enable them to deal more consciously with their own illness through psychoeducation.
In order to ensure that the online (D-)MCT fulfils the set goals, our study will examine the practical feasibility of the online format, the acceptance on the part of the participants, and the effectiveness with regard to the symptoms of the disease. For this purpose, information from the participants will be collected before the start of the intervention, as well as during its course, in the form of interviews and questionnaires. We assume that the online sessions of the MCT for psychosis, or the D-MCT, will be enjoyed by the participants and that the content will be well accepted due to the playful format. We also expect to see improvements in reported symptomatology and reported distress after completion of the modules.
	We consider the improvement of the quality of life of mentally ill persons to be the overriding goal of our scientific and therapeutic activities, and we would like to make our contribution to expanding the existing range of care.

interventions.name: Intervention: Subjects participate in group therapy in an online format.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Self-reported psychosis or depression 
Online informed consent 
Internet connection
Required devices available (PC with webcam, laptop, smartphone, or tablet)
Exclusion criteria:
Suicidal tendencies
Lack of group skills
lack of German language skills
